newsitem.title: USA: US corporate debt cable-focused, TCI scares Street.
newsitem.headline: US corporate debt cable-focused, TCI scares Street.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond trade for the second consecutive session found itself plagued by negative sentiments surrounding the credit status of TCI Communications, dealers said.
And high-yielding U.K. cable bonds dominated junk trade, lifted by merger news.

TCI debt widened from 10 to 20 basis points in active trade on Tuesday, traders said, doubling losses sustained in Monday's session. TCI's 6-7/8s of 2006 widened to a 220 basis point bid, 215 offer market, traders said, compared with a 205 bid late on Monday.

The downward spiral commenced after rating agency Standard & Poor's said late Friday it may lower TCI's debt ratings to junk bond status, dealers said. In its comment, S&P said the negative outlook reflected its concern that "debt relative to cash generation may remain at the outer edge of S&P's parameters for a marginal investment grade rating."

High-grades traders said the move has the entire market scared and has given them reason to reevaluate the entire sector. Traders were unwilling to forecast further widening in TCI debt, but most did expect the negative trend to continue.

Other cable and media debt was also quoted lower in sympathy with TCI, but only marginally by comparison. Time Warner's 7-3/4 percent notes due 2005 widened five basis points to 120 basis point spread, one trader said.
Separately, news that Viacom may pay MCA $1.45 billion and exchange its 50 percent interest in the Sci-Fi Channel for complete control of the USA Network weighed on related debt prices, traders said.
Outside cables, high-grades dealers said spreads were largely unchanged. Prices merely faded in line with U.S. Treasuries in light trade, they said.

May Department Stores' new issue of $125 million 20-year A2/single-A rated debentures widened slightly. The debt traded at a 65 basis point spread on Tuesday compared with Monday's initial level of 64, one trader said.

New issuance on Tuesday featured $200 million in Aa3/A-plus rated three-year notes from CIT Group Holdings via lead manager Smith Barney Inc. The notes were priced as 6-1/4s to yield 22 basis points over the Treasury curve.
One trader at a big New York shop contended the CIT notes were overpriced by about 10 basis points. The notes were not yet freed to trade.

Turning to high-yield activity, U.K. cable bonds were scattered higher after several large British cable and telecommunication companies announced they will merge their British operations. The deal, which involves the merger of Cable & Wireless Plc, NYNEX Corp of the U.S. and Bell Canada International, will create the largest U.K. cable operator.
Videotron zero coupon debt due 2005 rose more than five points to 72-3/4 bid, 73-3/4 offer into the close. The debt was quoted at 67 bid late on Monday.
TeleWest's zeros closed at 64 bid compared with a 62-1/2 bid at Monday's close. One high-yield trader said the bonds backed off from larger gains at midday, however.
International Cabletel closed at 61-1/8 bid, up from 58-1/2 closing bid on Monday.
U.S. high-yield telecommunication debt went south as it has for the past week, traders said, in response to what some traders called "too tight" spreads and negative industry news.
Arch Communications Group's zero coupon bonds dropped 5/8 point to 55-5/8 bid, 56 offer. Lenfest Communications' 10-1/2 percent debt closed at 99-1/4 bid, par offer against a 101-1/2 bid on Monday.
